fields.meta_description: Build a cake order form that sizes each cake by servings, prices delivery by distance, and sends the decorator every detail. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a Cake Order Form That Gives the Baker Every Detail
fields.hero_description: Build a cake order form that sizes each cake by guest count, prices delivery, and saves every order to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What Each Order Carries to the Kitchen
fields.features_subheading: Each question on the form replaces a phone call the baker would otherwise make before the first layer goes in the oven.
fields.feature_1:
Sizes listed by the servings they feed

Each size on the form shows how many people it serves and what it costs. A customer planning for 24 guests sees that a 10-inch round covers them and can pick it without calling.
fields.feature_2:
Flavor and filling asked once per tier

Every tier the customer adds brings its own questions about flavor and filling. The order then reads tier by tier, and the middle layer never gets the top layer's raspberry jam.
fields.feature_3:
Pickup dates that respect your notice

You set the notice each cake needs, such as 7 days for tiered cakes and 2 days for sheet cakes. The date picker then offers only dates the kitchen can still make in time.
fields.feature_4:
An alert for each new order

The app sends you an email or Slack alert when an order comes in, with the pickup date and size on the first line. A reminder goes to the customer the day before pickup.
fields.feature_5:
Orders in a database you own

Each order saves as a row in a database you own, with no response caps in your busiest week. Filter the rows by pickup date and the next day's bake list is ready to print.
fields.feature_6:
Your code, on GitHub if you want it

On paid plans, export the full code of the form and its order database to your GitHub repository. A developer can then host it alongside your bakery's site or add features.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Bakeries, Four Kinds of Cake Order
fields.tab_content_1:
For 140 guests, three tiers that serve 150

Sugarline Cake Studio sizes every wedding cake from the guest count. Imani Achebe and Lukas Brandt enter 140 guests, and the form suggests three tiers serving 150 at $6 a serving. The $900 quote appears before they book a tasting, and Imani picks lemon with raspberry for the bottom tier.
fields.tab_content_2:
Every letter of the message, exactly as typed

Parents ordering from Brindle Oven Bakery type the message to pipe on top, up to 30 characters, and upload a photo of the design they like. Gemma Hollis orders an 8-inch chocolate cake reading Happy 7th Birthday, Otis. The decorator's ticket shows her message letter for letter, next to her photo.
fields.tab_content_3:
Call-backs for every nut allergy order

Hazelbrook Bakehouse bakes almond cakes on a shared bench, so its form never confirms a nut allergy order by itself. When Dev Raman ticks a tree nut allergy for a Saturday birthday cake, the order button becomes a call-back request. Owner Marisol Ybarra gets it by email and calls him before accepting.
fields.tab_content_4:
Each mile past 10 adds $2 to delivery

Saltbox Cake Co. delivers within 10 miles for $20 and charges $2 for each mile beyond that. Paloma Reyes enters a venue 16 miles away for her sister's engagement party. The form adds $32 for delivery to her $380 cake and shows a $412 total before she sends the order.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Cake Order Form
fields.howto_description: Follow these seven steps to turn your size chart and delivery rules into a cake order form for your bakery.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 List your sizes and what each feeds
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Decide what each tier can carry
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write down every size you bake, the number of servings each one feeds, and its price. Mark the sizes that can stack into tiers. This chart becomes the size question, and it lets the form suggest a size when a customer gives a guest count.
fields.howto_step_2_des: List the flavors and fillings you offer and mark the ones that cost extra, such as a fresh fruit filling. Choose whether a customer picks one flavor for the whole cake or one for each tier. That choice sets how many times the form asks.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Ask for the message to pipe with a character limit that fits your smallest cake top. Add an upload for a reference photo and a short field for colors. Give your decorator a picture to work from, not a paragraph describing one.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Write a plain-English description of the form: your size chart, the tier choices, the notice each cake needs, and your delivery rate. Emergent builds a working form from that description, pricing included.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Add the rules that change an order
fields.howto_step_5_des: Ask for each rule in a sentence, such as a longer notice period for wedding cakes, or a separate flavor list for gluten-free sponges. Change any rule later by prompting Emergent again.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Place a test order as a customer
fields.howto_step_6_des: Order a cake from the published form with a long message and a delivery address. Check that the price matches your chart, that the new-order alert reaches you, and that the decorator's ticket matches what you entered.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Share the link where customers ask
fields.howto_step_7_des: Put the form link on your bakery's website and in your social profiles, and send it in reply to anyone who asks for a cake by message. Every order then lands in one place instead of across several inboxes.

faq_plan.q: What is a cake order form?
faq_plan.a: A cake order form is what a bakery uses to take a cake order before baking it: what the cake should be, when and where it is needed, and how to reach the customer. An online cake order form can also price the cake from the size and delivery answers while the customer fills it in.

faq_plan.q: How to make a bakery order form?
faq_plan.ref: How to make a bakery order form?

prov.original: How to make a bakery order form?

faq_plan.a: Start with what you sell and what each size costs. Then list what you must know before baking, such as the date and any allergies. Describe all of it to Emergent's AI form builder in plain English, and Emergent builds the form with its pricing and a database for the orders. Change any question later by prompting.

faq_plan.q: What questions should a cake order form ask?
faq_plan.hint: How to create a cake order form?
faq_plan.a: Ask for the event date and the guest count first: the date tells you whether the kitchen has room, and the count sets the size. Then ask for flavor and filling, the design with a reference photo, the message to pipe, allergies, pickup or delivery, and a phone number. Leave out anything that changes neither the cake nor the price.

faq_plan.q: Can a cake order form print a ticket for the decorator?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Have the form lay each order out as a one-page ticket, and sort the day's tickets by pickup time. It plays the role a work order form plays in a repair shop: one sheet carries the whole job to the person doing it. Ask Emergent for the ticket layout in the same prompt as the form.

faq_plan.q: How much notice should a cake order form require?
faq_plan.a: Set the notice per cake type instead of one number for the whole menu, and use the lead time your kitchen needs for each. Give a three-tier wedding cake its own notice period, apart from the sheet cakes. For a date inside the notice, offer a call-back instead of checkout and decide each rush request yourself.

faq_plan.q: How should a cake order form handle allergy requests?
faq_plan.a: Use a checklist of allergens, not a free-text box, and name on the form the allergens your kitchen already bakes with. Decide in advance what each ticked box does to the order. Print any ticked allergen at the top of the decorator's ticket in bold, where nobody at the bench can miss it.

faq_plan.q: Can a cake order form also take cupcake orders?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Open the form with a product choice and show only the questions each product needs: tiers and servings for a cake, a flavor per dozen for cupcakes. If cookies sell by the dozen on their own pickup days, a separate cookie order form keeps those rules out of the cake orders.

faq_plan.q: How do I make a simple cake order form that works on a phone?
faq_plan.a: Put one question on each screen and keep the first screen to the date and the guest count. Emergent can build the form as a conversational flow with one question per screen. Keep the photo upload optional, because some customers will only have an idea, not a picture.

faq_plan.q: How do I stop a cake order form from overbooking a weekend?
faq_plan.a: Cap the cakes per pickup day, or the servings per day if large cakes take most of your oven time, and have the form stop offering a date once it is full. Write the cap into your prompt to Emergent in plain English, and raise it by prompting when you add staff. A full date then drops out of the date picker until an order on it is canceled.

faq_plan.q: Can I reuse a cake order form for other made-to-order products?
faq_plan.a: You can, because its structure carries over: what is being made, the options that change the price, a due date, and how it reaches the customer. A t shirt order form, for example, swaps servings for sizes and flavors for colors, and still shows the total before the order is sent.
